analysis.title: US Equities Mid-Day Color (GS Equities Mid-Day Color, 2 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Breadth-led relief rally after last week's selloff: 374 S&P 500 names green and the equal-weight S&P (SPW) up 1%, outrunning the S&P 500 at +30bps on session highs.

Volume is about 12% above the 20-day average to start the month, but the desk says it does not feel like an all-clear because the market reversed off session highs and could not hold earlier gains despite more positive Mideast headlines.
AI trade is stabilizing: Mag7 modestly higher and trying to snap a 3-week losing streak for the first time since March. AMZN +4% leads the group, AAPL lags ahead of tonight's earnings.
Semis are modestly lower after briefly reclaiming the 200-day moving average (10,796), following Friday's first close below it since June 2025.
Momentum factor is down 5.5% and at a 1-year low. Winners are down 2.5% and Losers up 3% as geopolitical tensions ease and energy sells off.
Crowded positioning is holding up: the GS HF Performance basket (GSTHVIPP) is up 60bps to start the month.

Prime brokerage recap for Friday: US equities were net sold, with short selling outpacing long buying 2.7 to 1. Fundamental managers trimmed losses on the end-of-day bounce, Quants slipped further and Multi-Strats finished flat.
On the week, hedge funds net bought US equities for the first time in 4 weeks, driven by short covering in Macro Products and to a lesser extent Single Stocks.
Info Tech was the most net bought sector last week (through Thursday) but was still heavily net sold in October. Mag 7 names collectively were net sold in 4 of the last 5 sessions.

GS Sector Specialists published 22 durable ideas built around post-midterm clearing events and seasonality: Housing (SHW low torque, BLDR high torque), Defense (RTX, LMT), Financial compounders (JPM, APO, EVR), and Retail (+7.3% average in November, 80% hit rate). Fades: NKE, LULU, PEP, GIS.

GS franchise flows are up 11% vs the 2-week average. Long-only clients are 6% better for sale (Info Tech, Health Care, Comm Svcs outweigh demand for Financials, Industrials, Cons Disc). Hedge funds are 12% better to buy (Tech, Industrials, Health Care, Financials), net for sale only in Comm Svcs.
Chart of the day: the ETF inflow theme is intact and shows no signs of slowing.
